video.description:
🔥 Oh God of Jabez, hear my cry today and help me! 🙏✨ Begin this powerful prayer session with faith, humility, and expectation. Inspired by the biblical prayer of Jabez and teachings associated with Apostle Joshua Selman, this Christian prayer is designed to help you seek God’s mercy, favor, protection, guidance, strength, and divine intervention. 📖🕊️

🙏 Cry out to God with faith
🔥 Ask God to enlarge your territory
🛡️ Seek divine protection from evil
✨ Pray for favor and open doors
🙌 Trust God in difficult situations
❤️ Surrender your burdens into His hands

Take time to pray and meditate on God’s Word. 🌅📖 Let this powerful prayer encourage you to seek God wholeheartedly and believe that He can transform your circumstances.

Subscribe to Grace & Glory Prayers 🔔 for powerful Christian prayers, Bible-based encouragement, daily devotionals, and faith-building messages. 🙏✨

Grace & Glory Prayers is an independent channel and is not officially affiliated with Apostle Joshua Selman.

transcript.text: I want to speak directly to whatever name has been spoken over your life before we go one sentence, father.
Because I believe some of you have been living inside a name you never chose.
Carrying its weight into every room you enter, letting it quietly determine what you believe you are actually allowed to become.
I need you to hear something this morning.
A name given to you in someone else's pain does not have to become the prophecy over your entire future.
First Chronicles chapter 4 verse 9 gives us the account I want to plant into your spirit.
And Jabes was more honorable than his brethren, and his mother called his name Jabes saying, because I bare him with sorrow.
I want you to sit with the weight of this verse before we move a single step, father.
Jabes means sorrow or pain, depending on how the Hebrew is rendered.
And his own mother gave him that name deliberately, marking him permanently with the memory of whatever labor, whatever grief,
whatever difficulties surrounded his birth.
Every time anyone called his name for the rest of his life, they were unknowingly speaking a word associated with pain directly over him.
And yet the very same verse tells us something that should stop you cold with its implications.
He was more honorable than his brethren.
Not despite the name attached to him.
The text does not describe a man who overcame his name through decades of struggle before finally achieving some measure of respect late in life.

It presents the honor and the name side by side, as though scripture wants you to understand from the very first mention of this man that a painful name and an honorable life are not actually incompatible outcomes.
I decree over you this morning, whatever name has been spoken over your life, whether given carelessly by a bitter parent,
whether inherited through a family history steeped in genuine tragedy,
whether self-assigned through years of internalizing other people's disappointed expectations of you, does not carry the final authority over what you are permitted to become.
Jabes's name never stop being sorrow.
What changed was not the name, what changed was the trajectory of the life carrying it.
I feel something rising even in the middle of this teaching.
There is someone reading or hearing this exact sentence who has quietly accepted a specific label as their permanent identity.
The difficult child, the family disappointment, the one everyone expected less from,
the one whose very existence was framed by someone's careless words as burden rather than blessing.
I speak to that specific internalized name this morning, it does not get the final word over your life.
Jabes did not need his name erased to become honorable, he needed something else entirely, and we're about to discover exactly what that was.
Let the fire climb higher because verse 10 gives us the exact mechanism that shifted Jabes's trajectory.
